# THE RULES, QUOTED FROM THE CANONICAL VALIDATOR

#   2. Every commit in FIRST..CLOSE has ACT=<same id> with a valid
#   4. Exactly one CLOSE exists in FIRST..CLOSE and it is the last
#   6. No commit after CLOSE carries ACT=<id>.
# RULE 6 IS ENFORCED OVER THE WHOLE DESCENDANT PATH, not merely over
#   The rule is about the whole DESCENDANT PATH of CLOSE, so the check
#   now walks every commit reachable from CLOSE (excluding CLOSE
#   itself) and rejects any of them that carries ACT:<id>.
#   THE SET OF COMMITS CARRYING ACT:<id> IS EXACTLY THE SET
#   FIRST..CLOSE, AND CLOSE IS ITS LAST MEMBER.
# CONSEQUENCE. A commit that carries ACT:<id> may NOT be created after
# the terminal close. The terminality receipt therefore CANNOT be
# recorded under the ACT id, and CANNOT be recorded before the close
